source_inspections.origin_group: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
source_inspections.evidence_extract: The published opinion in No. 25-9548 denied Pawnee Nation’s petition and affirmed EPA’s interpretation of SAFETEA §10211(a). The majority held that the provision remains active, requires approval when its conditions are met and supported Oklahoma’s administration of 26 programs under six federal environmental statutes. The opinion records EPA’s May 12, 2025 removal of a State-Tribal Engagement Condition and Judge Federico’s dissent.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: Reuters independently reported the 2-1 ruling, EPA’s 2025 approval of Oklahoma authority over environmental programs in Indian country and the dissent’s tribal-sovereignty concerns. The report did not convert the ruling into a finding about later environmental outcomes.
source_inspections.hash_scope: SHA-256 of the exact normalized evidence extract retained below, not a claim of hashing the publisher’s complete webpage.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: Reuters reviewed a summary of an internal ICAO assistance report sent to Lebanon in September. It reported expired conditional airport certification, no emergency plan, inadequate long-haul firefighting resources, licensing-inspector gaps and no fully operational independent accident-investigation authority. Minister Fayez Rasamny acknowledged most issues, described corrective work and said certification was expected; FAA declined comment and no direct service had resumed.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: Reuters reported Trump’s July directive to allow U.S. carriers to fly directly to Lebanon and FAA’s named statement that it would work with carriers and agencies under appropriate safety conditions. The report stated that an extensive airport security review and safety certification would be required before service could resume.
